pr.title: Let an agent withdraw an inbox item through a tool
pr.head: c42758ebd6e7369087c7d2871708346da9da6e06

summary: Projector's inbox lets an agent post a question (with ask) or a notice (with tell) that waits for the person in the band, the list Projector's Claude Code plugin draws above the prompt. When the person answers or dismisses a question, a deliverer sends an ANSWER or DISMISSED line back to the agent that asked.

Agents also need to clear items that went stale, such as a question the person answered in the conversation. Until now the generated AGENTS.md section told them to run project inbox list and project inbox dismiss from the shell on every message. That cost a shell command each time, and a dismissal looked like the person's own: it sent a DISMISSED line back to the agent and stayed in the band, struck through, for 30 seconds.

This pull request adds a third action, withdraw. project inbox withdraw <number> runs the same locked write as dismiss, adds withdrawn: true to the answer, and marks the item delivered at once, so no deliverer sends anything back. The plugin registers a matching withdraw tool (mcp__projector__withdraw), and the band drops a withdrawn item immediately. Version 10 of the AGENTS.md section tells agents to use the tool.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Band: the list of pull requests and inbox items the Claude Code plugin shows above the prompt.
  • Item: a question or a notice, stored as one JSON file per number in the session's inbox directory.
  • Delivered: deliveredAt is set, so no deliverer (watch or the band) sends the item's answer to the agent again.
  • Withdrawn: dismissed by the agent that posted it, recorded as {dismissed, withdrawn, answeredAt} and delivered at once.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first Projector review of cb692b0 was clean, with no finding threads, and suggested that answer stop refusing a withdrawn question as already answered. c42758e takes that suggestion, and an incremental review of it is clean.

groups.title: The withdraw command
groups.kicker: The CLI records a withdrawal as a dismissal that is already delivered
intro: Withdrawing reuses dismiss, which finds the item, checks that it is still open, and writes it under the session's lock. A withdrawn flag adds one field to the stored answer and sets deliveredAt to the same moment. Because the item is delivered, watch and the band's deliverer skip it, and list without --all leaves it out.
Refusals now say how an item was resolved. Before, dismiss, snooze, and answer told a caller that a dismissed question was already answered, as 3, which would tell an agent the person had answered.

files.note: dismiss takes withdrawn; the new resolution names how an item was resolved in the refusals of dismiss, snooze, and answer.

checks.text: A withdrawn question is delivered at once. In a scratch store, withdraw 1 followed by watch --once printed nothing, and list --all showed the item as withdrawn.

Answering a withdrawn or dismissed question now says already withdrawn or already dismissed. test_answering_a_withdrawn_or_dismissed_question_says_which passed at this head, and the band acts on the exit code, not the message.

files.note: Adds the withdraw subcommand on dismiss's code path, and shows a withdrawn item's state as withdrawn.

groups.title: The withdraw tool and the band
groups.kicker: Claude Code's agent withdraws through a tool, and the band drops the item at once
intro: The plugin's hooks module registers withdraw beside ask and tell. A call runs project inbox withdraw <number> --session <id> --json, puts the printed item in the band's list, closes the item's drawer if it is open, and tells the agent nothing comes back.

The three tools now share one runner, runTool. It passes exit 65 (refused), 66 (no such item), and 75 (store busy) back as the CLI's message, and tells the agent to run project upgrade on any other failure, such as an old CLI without withdraw.

In the band, isShownAt leaves out a withdrawn item. A dismissal the person makes stays for 30 seconds, struck through, to confirm their own action; a withdrawal is not their action, so it leaves at once.

checks.text: Exit 66 is new to the runner's pass-through list. ask and tell never look up an item, so they never exit 66, and their behavior is unchanged.

files.note: A Dismissal type with an optional withdrawn, shared by questions and notices.
The tool's description, schema, and withdrawArguments; isShownAt leaves out a withdrawn item.

checks.text: The band's other readers of answer (the new-item check in setItems, the open counts, and the drawers) treat a withdrawn item as a resolved dismissal, so hiding it here is the only change they need. Traced in hooks/register.tsx.

files.note: Registers three tools in one loop, renames post to runTool, and adds the withdraw hook.

checks.text: The hook replaces the item from the CLI's output before the band reads the store again, so the line and its drawer disappear as soon as the tool returns.

groups.title: Instructions and documentation
groups.kicker: Version 10 of the AGENTS.md section, the reference docs, and plan section 12
intro: project init writes a generated Projector section into each repository's AGENTS.md, and refreshes it when the template's version moves. Version 10 replaces the shell commands with the withdraw tool and drops the step that listed items on every message: the agent's own conversation already holds each number ask or tell returned.
The inbox plan's new section 12 records the design. The project stays in-progress, because a manual check from section 4 is still open.
